item.title: Tripod Reordering: A 33-Queue Layout of Planar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A queue layout of a graph consists of a linear order of the vertices and a partition of the edges into queues so that no two edges in a single queue are nested. The minimum number of queues needed in a queue layout of a graph is called its queue number. A planar product structure theorem of Dujmovi\'c, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt, and Wood (JACM, 2020) states that every planar graph is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph of simple treewidth at most $3$, a clique $K_3$, and a path. The result has been used to show that the queue number of planar graphs is at most $49$. Recently, Bekos, Gronemann, and Raftopoulou (Algorithmica, 2023) investigated how the general approach based on the product structure can be optimized for planar graphs. They claim that an appropriate reordering of the three vertices associated with each bag in the product structure decomposition, called a tripod, reduces the queue number of planar graphs to $42$. We first highlight a gap in their queue layout algorithm: one of the choices required by the algorithm is not guaranteed to exist. Then we show how to address the limitation and provide an alternative tripod reordering mechanism that reduces the upper bound on the queue number of planar graphs to $33$. As a corollary, bipartite planar graphs have queue number at most $22$.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Pupyrev

item.title: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, we say that a set $A\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ is an $(r,c)$ subspace evasive set if and only if for any affine subspace $U\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ with bounded dimension $\dim(U)\leq r$, the intersection size $|A\cap U|$ is at most $c$. The probabilistic method shows the existence of $(r,c)$ subspace evasive sets with $|A| = q^{(1-\epsilon) n}$ with $c = O(r/\epsilon)$. However, the best explicit constructions by Dvir--Lovett (STOC 2012) and Ben-Aroya--Shinkar (CJTCS 2013) have $c$ growing as an exponential function of $r$. Here, we give an explicit construction of such subspace evasive set that achieves the intersection bound $c=O(\min(r\log(r/\epsilon)/\epsilon, r^2/\epsilon))$ when both $r$ and $1/\epsilon$ are constants. Our approach is simple and the key idea is to compose subspace design codes (Guruswami-Xing, STOC 2013) with a suitably chosen ``local'' subspace evasive set. As a corollary, we give the first construction of an explicit (strongly) capacity-achieving list-recoverable code with nearly optimal list size, circumventing all previously-known barriers to construction.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Mahdi Cheraghchi, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami, Aaron Putterman, Zihan Zhang

item.title: Constrained intersection representations and forbidden patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.16849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the interplay between two types of graph classes: the ones defined by intersections of geometric objects and the ones defined by the absence of a substructure. More precisely, we study intersection graphs that are grounded, that is, the objects lie above a horizontal line that they touch, and ordered graphs with forbidden patterns, that is, ordered graphs that avoid a set of ordered induced subgraphs. These two approaches are fundamentally different, but it is known that several interesting graph classes have both types of characterizations, and we aim to understand whether this is a general phenomenon. Our contributions are the following. First, we identify a family of patterns on four vertices and a natural hierarchy of intersection graphs of strings whose classes are nicely interleaved. This raises hopes to prove connections between the two perspectives. Second, we dampen these hopes by proving that a class of (ordered) intersection graphs that we study cannot be characterized by a finite set of forbidden patterns. Third, we show a dual impossibility result: there exists a pattern-defined class of our hierarchy that admits no intersection representation, if we require this representation to be closed under natural operations such as translation and scaling. However, it turns out that if we allow slightly more exotic intersection representations, then we can find one for this pattern-defined class.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Feuilloley, Michel Habib, Amalia Sorondo

item.title: Nonlinear lower-tail large deviations at criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.10233v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce general methods to derive lower tail large deviation principles, for a variety of nonlinear problems of combinatorial interest. These methods are especially effective in "critical" regimes, where the nonlinearities are not sparse enough for Poissonian lower tails (e.g., Janson's inequality does not provide a sharp tail bound), but the situation is not so dense that combinatorial effects dominate (e.g., we cannot directly apply the theory of hypergraph containers or the relative entropy framework of Kozma-Samotij). In particular, these are regimes where one expects interesting phase transitions to occur. Our results have a number of consequences related to subgraphs in random graphs, answering various questions of Warnke and Jenssen-Perkins-Potukuchi-Simkin. For example, consider a random graph $G\sim \mathbb G(n,p)$, and let $L_\triangle(n,p)=\log\Pr[G\text{ is triangle-free}]$. The first-order asymptotics of $L_\triangle(n,p)$ have long been known in all parameter ranges except the critical regime where $p$ has order of magnitude $1/\sqrt n$. We are able to fill this gap: for any fixed $c>0$, we show that $n^{-3/2}L_\triangle(n,c/\sqrt n)$ converges to a limit expressed in terms of a two-parameter variational problem, which has a single phase transition at $c\approx 4.341$. In contrast, we show that there is no such phase transition for the probability that $G$ is $C_{2\ell}$-free, for any fixed even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. We also obtain some applications in combinatorial design theory. Addressing conjectures of Glock-K\"uhn-Lo-Osthus, Kelly, and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin, we obtain new estimates on the number of order-$n$ Steiner triple systems with no Pasch configuration and the number of order-$n$ Latin squares with no $2\times 2$ Latin subsquare (both tight up to a factor of $\exp(o(n^2))$).
item.dc:creator: Matthew Kwan, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT. Prompted by this ready conversion of (P)STS to 3-CNF formulas and numerous real-world applications of (P)STS, we explore the intersection of (P)STS with 3-SAT and its counting version \#3-SAT. We explain the properties of (P)STS-generated 3-CNF formulas in terms familiar to the SAT community and experimentally compare them against randomly-generated 3-CNF formulas. We find that PSTS-3-CNF formulas are statistically distinct from randomly generated 3-CNF formulas, in both probability of satisfiability and expected solution count.
item.dc:creator: Wyatt Olson, Jared Soundy, J. Z. Schroeder

item.title: Sublogarithmic Online Graph Exploration
item.description: arXiv:2611.14827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the online graph exploration problem, in which an agent must visit every vertex of an initially unknown weighted graph on $n$ vertices and return to its starting vertex. In this model, a vertex's incident edges and their weights are revealed when it is first visited. Despite extensive research, the best known competitive guarantee for general graphs had remained $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$, a bound already established in 1977 for the greedy TSP heuristic Nearest Neighbor. Subsequent approaches, including hierarchical depth-first search (hDFS) and Blocking, achieve better guarantees on restricted graph classes but have logarithmic or worse competitive ratios on general graphs. This raises the question of whether the logarithmic barrier is inherent and Nearest Neighbor is asymptotically optimal. We answer this question in the negative by giving an $\mathcal{O}(\log n/\log \log n)$-competitive algorithm. Our algorithm is a slight modification of hDFS, and we establish its competitive guarantee with a surprisingly short proof.
item.dc:creator: Julia Baligacs

item.title: Small classes have linear neighbourhood complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.15299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A hereditary graph class is small if it contains at most $n!c^n$ labelled graphs on $n$ vertices for some constant $c$. Small classes include proper minor-closed classes and classes of bounded twin-width. We prove that every small class has linear neighbourhood complexity, that is, in every graph in the class, vertex neighbourhoods intersect any $k$-vertex set in only $O(k)$ distinct ways. This resolves a conjecture of Bonnet, Duron, and the first two authors (ITCS 2025) and makes the algorithmic, structural, and representation consequences of linear neighbourhood complexity available for every small class. In particular, every small class admits an adjacency labelling scheme with $O(\log^2 n)$-bit labels, improving the previous $O(\log^3 n)$ bound.
item.dc:creator: John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev, Maksim Zhukovskii

item.title: Integrality Gap of 3.4 for Santa Claus: A Topology-based Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.15392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the \textsc{Max-Min Allocation} problem, a set of indivisible items are to be assigned to a set of players and the goal is to maximize the minimum value among all players. A much studied special case, the \textsc{Santa Claus} problem, assumes that an item has a fixed utility but a player is only interested in a subset of items. The main technique for designing approximation algorithms for \textsc{Santa Claus} is the configuration LP, introduced by the Bansal and Sviridenko. A long line of research has progressively improved the upper bound of the integrality gap, mostly relying on the combinatorial arguments of Haxell for finding perfect matchings in certain hypergraphs. Remarkably, a recent paper of Haxell and Szab\'o (SODA '23) introduced a novel topology-based analysis, by which they are able to obtain the current best upper bound of $3.534$. In this work, we adapt the approach of Haxell and Szab\'o to analyze the integrality gap. The main new ingredient in our adaptation is that we stop the process of "edge explosions" in a graph used by Haxell and Szab\'o when it becomes too costly. This early termination of explosions, combined with a new lower bound on a topological connectivity parameter based on a theorem of Aharoni, Berger, and Meshulam, allows us to improve the integrality gap to $3.4$. Our analysis has the additional advantage of being simpler.
item.dc:creator: Kimon Boehmer, Chien-Chung Huang

item.title: Asymptotically Optimal Bounds for Counting Near-Minimum Circuits in Regular Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.15755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a regular matroid on $m$ elements with positive weights and weighted girth $g_w$, we prove that the number of circuits of weight at most $\alpha g_w$ is bounded by $(Km)^{2\alpha}$, for every real $\alpha\ge1$ and an absolute constant $K$. This improves the previous $m^{O(\alpha^2)}$ bound of Gurjar and Vishnoi and matches classic graph cut and cycle counting bounds of Karger and Subramanian. We also show this is asymptotically optimal for all real $\alpha\geq 1$ under the Erd\H{o}s girth conjecture, while unconditional optimality holds for half-integer $\alpha$ by prior results. As consequences, we resolve a recent conjecture by Khanna, Putterman, and Song implying the existence of a parallel basis search algorithm for regular matroids terminating in logarithmically many rounds of independence queries, and obtain improved bounds on the number of near-minimum weight codewords in regular codes and near-shortest vectors in totally unimodular lattices under $\ell_p$-norms.
item.dc:creator: Robert P. Streit

item.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS) at 33 Orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.16299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Latin square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array over symbols $\{0,1,\ldots n-1\}$, such that the same symbol does not appear twice in any row or any column. Two Latin squares of order $n$ are orthogonal if, when superimposed, they yield each of the $n^2$ ordered pairs of symbols exactly once. A set of two or more Latin squares are mutually orthogonal Latin squares (MOLS) if each pair of distinct squares is orthogonal. Let $N(n)$ be the maximum size of a set of MOLS of order $n$. For most $n$ which are not prime powers, there is a wide gap between known upper and lower bounds on $N(n)$. This has led to interest in constructing new larger sets of MOLS for explicit values of $n$, to incrementally improve the lower bounds on $N(n)$. This paper provides MOLS that improve the lower bound on $N(n)$ for 33 values of $n$ in the range from 22 through 494. The constructions were found by GPT-6 Astra, and use established techniques including difference matrices, quasi-difference matrices, orthogonal arrays, and projective planes. A highlight is 4 MOLS of order $n=22$; combined with pre-existing results, this establishes $N(n) \geq 4$ for all $n>10$.
item.dc:creator: Christopher D. Rosin

item.title: When Elements Fail: Weighted Fault-Tolerant Matroid Bases
item.description: arXiv:2611.16333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a rank-\(r\) matroid on \(n\) elements with nonnegative costs and a partition into safe and vulnerable elements, we seek a minimum-cost set that spans after every deletion of at most \(k\) selected vulnerable elements. We resolve several open questions posed by Bentert, Fomin, Golovach, and Morelle (ESA 2025) concerning weighted costs, nonuniform failures, and explicitly specified failure scenarios. To this end, we develop two compression methods. For matroids given by an independence oracle, weighted flat-avoidance representatives yield a bounded subset of the ground set containing an optimal solution and a \(2^{\mathcal{O}((r+k)^4)}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\)-time algorithm. This establishes fixed-parameter tractability for weighted costs and nonuniform failures simultaneously. For explicitly represented linear matroids, polynomial certificates allow us to compress families of partial solutions while preserving successful completions under all allowed failures. This yields a deterministic algorithm using \(2^{\mathcal{O}(kr(r+k)\log(r+1))}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\) field operations over arbitrary fields. Over fixed finite fields, a simpler reduction uses parallel classes. For explicitly listed failure scenarios, we obtain fixed-parameter algorithms parameterized by rank and the number of scenarios. In contrast, the size-budget decision version is W[1]-hard parameterized by rank and maximum scenario size, even on uniform matroids with two-element scenarios. \keywords{Matroids \and Fault tolerance \and Fixed-parameter algorithms \and Representative families}
item.dc:creator: Madhumita Kundu, Soumi Nandi, Saket Saurabh

item.title: Explicit Edit Codes via Multicoloring
item.description: arXiv:2611.16835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any fixed integers $q\ge2$ and $t\ge1$, we construct explicit $q$-ary codes of length $n$ that correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions, with redundancy at most $2t\log_q n+O_{q,t}(\log\log n)$ $q$-ary symbols. This matches the leading redundancy term of Levenshtein's classical existential bound. Building on the standard graph-coloring approach, we use a prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph to assign multiple colors to each $q$-ary word of length $m<n$. Appending a short, edit-protected representation of an assigned color to the length-$m$ word yields a length-$n$ codeword. The choice among the assigned colors carries additional message information, thereby reducing the redundancy. The construction admits deterministic encoding and decoding in $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{6t+2})$ and $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{7t+2})$ time, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Huiling Xie, Zitan Chen

item.title: An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
item.description: arXiv:2611.16839v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question. For an $n$-dimensional corner polyhedron associated with an integer lattice of determinant $\delta$, the number of edges is at most $$ O\left(n6^n \cdot \bigl(1+\log_2(2\delta)\bigr)^{2n-3}\right). $$ This improves the standard bound obtained by counting pairs of vertices, reducing the logarithmic exponent from $(2n-2)$ to $(2n-3)$.
item.dc:creator: A. Yu. Chirkov, S. I. Veselov, D. V. Gribanov, D. S. Malyshev, N. Yu. Zolotykh

item.title: Optimal Polyomino Fences
item.description: arXiv:2611.16883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The $n$-omino fence problem asks how many cells can be surrounded by placing every $n$-omino exactly once in the grid. We present a new dynamic programming approach for this problem, allowing us to prove optimality for the pentomino and hexomino fence and to classify all possible pentomino orders by optimal area. For the first time we also provide strong heuristic solutions and upper bounds for all fences up to $n = 15$, after which we even approximate the $500$-omino fence with computational experiments. Finally, we generalize the problem to 3D, where we prove optimality for pentacubes and derive heuristic solutions for hexacubes and heptacubes.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Langlois-R\'emillard, Mia N. M\"u{\ss}ig, Helmut Podhaisky, Erika Roldan, G\"unter Rote, Maximilian Br\"omme, Matthes Norden, Maximilian Prietzel, Daniel Yu, Mykhailo Lyader

item.title: Large diameter for $(\Delta+2)$-colouring reconfiguration
item.description: arXiv:2611.17022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2\mu$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + \mu$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $\mu$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}\mu-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $\Delta$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} \mu$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.
item.dc:creator: Wouter Cames van Batenburg

item.title: New bounds on the boxicity of Kneser graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a graph $G=(V,E)$, the boxicity $\operatorname{box}(G)$ is the least integer $d$ such that $G$ is the intersection graph of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ is the graph whose vertex set corresponds to the family of $k$ sized subsets of an $n$ sized ground set, and a pair of vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding sets are disjoint. In this short paper, we provide new bounds for the boxicity of $K(n,k)$. We first show that for $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 2k+1$, $\operatorname{box}(K(n,k))\ge n-2k$, thereby improving the lower bounds of Caoduro and Lichev [Discrete Mathematics 346(5):113333 (2023)] when $n\geq 3k+1$ and $k\ge 3$. The proof of this result uses the topological method and follows a strategy similar to Greene's proof of the Kneser's conjecture on the chromatic number of $K(n,k)$. We also show that for $k\ge 2$, $t\ge 1$ and $n=2k+t$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+t,k)) \leq O( t^3\log(2k+t) ).$ In particular, for every $t=t(k)\ge1$ with $t^3\log k=o(k)$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+t,k))=o(k)$. This is the first upper bound on the boxicity of $K(n,k)$ that is sublinear in $n$. We also show that for large enough $k$, $\operatorname{box}(K(2k+1,k))\le \frac{3\ln (2k+1)}{\ln\ln (2k+1)}$.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Suraj Kumar Sahoo

item.title: Triameter, distance packings, and vertex connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study upper bounds for the triameter of a connected graph in terms of distance packings and vertex connectivity. For any positive integer $k$, we bound the triameter of a graph by a linear function of its $k$-packing number and show that this bound is tight for all values of the parameters. As a corollary, we confirm the conjecture of Das and Abdio\u{g}lu on the upper bound for the triameter in terms of the order and the minimum degree of a graph. We also find the maximum triameter among graphs with given order and vertex connectivity, and describe the extremal graphs. Our main tool is a projection of a graph onto a spider or a unicyclic graph which preserves the distances between three prescribed vertices.
item.dc:creator: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko

item.title: Word-representability and comparability: Minimal forbidden induced subgraphs and cover number bounds
item.description: arXiv:2502.06979v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Word-representable graphs, characterized by the existence of a semi-transitive orientation, form a well-studied class of graphs. Comparability graphs form another well-studied class and constitute a subclass of word-representable graphs. Both classes are hereditary and admit characterizations in terms of minimal forbidden induced subgraphs. While the minimal forbidden induced subgraphs for comparability graphs are completely characterized, the corresponding characterization for word-representable graphs remains open. In this paper, we precisely determine which minimal non-comparability graphs are also minimal non-word-representable graphs by classifying minimal non-comparability graphs according to whether they are word-representable. As a consequence, we provide a complete description of minimal non-word-representable graphs containing an all-adjacent vertex. We also address an open problem posed by Kenkireth et al.\ concerning the cover number of word-representable graphs by comparability graphs. We demonstrate the existence of word-representable graphs on $n$ vertices whose cover number by comparability graphs is $\Omega(\log n)$, which establishes that the universal $O(\log n)$ upper bound is asymptotically tight for the class of word-representable graphs. For triangle-free circle graphs, we establish that the cover number by comparability graphs is at most $3$ and demonstrate that this bound is tight. More generally, we show that for any circle graph $G$ with clique number $\omega(G)$, the cover number by comparability graphs is bounded by $O(\log \omega(G))$. Finally, we identify four subclasses of word-representable graphs for which the cover number by comparability graphs of every graph in these classes is at most $2$.
item.dc:creator: Benny George Kenkireth, Gopalan Sajith, Sreyas Sasidharan

item.title: The Path-Extremal Conjecture for Zero Forcing: Distance-Hereditary Graphs and a Split-Decomposition Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2605.10836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A zero-forcing set of a graph is a set for which, after regarding each of its vertices as being blue, and applying the rule that a blue vertex with exactly one white neighbor forces said neighbor to become blue, all of the vertices in the graph are blue. Let $z(G;k)$ denote the number of zero forcing sets of size $k$. A conjecture of Boyer et al.\ asserts that the path $P_n$ maximizes these numbers coefficientwise among all $n$-vertex graphs. We prove this path-extremal conjecture for distance-hereditary graphs, which is the class of all graphs $G$ such that for each of the connected induced subgraphs of $G$, the distances between any two vertices in that subgraph are the same as they are in $G$. This extends the previously known tree case in which the path-extremal conjecture was known to be true to a much larger class that includes, in particular, all trees and all cographs. We then use canonical split decomposition to push the argument we used to show the distance-hereditary result into the more general setting of a connected graph with at most one prime bag in its canonical split decomposition. Specifically, we show that if a split-prime graph $H$ and all of its induced subgraphs are path-extremal, then every connected graph whose canonical split decomposition has a unique prime bag whose label graph is isomorphic to $H$ is also path-extremal. As a corollary of this result, for each fixed $m$, if every induced subgraph of every split-prime graph on at most $m$ vertices is path-extremal, then so is every connected graph whose canonical split decomposition has a unique prime bag of size at most $m$. Additionally, we prove that the path-extremal conjecture holds when all prime bags have order at most six, without restricting their number; under the preceding hereditary hypothesis, one additional prime bag labelled by $H$ is also allowed.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 32nd International Computing and Combinatorics Conference (COCOON 2026), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16835, pp. 409-422, Springer (2027)
item.dc:creator: Samuel German

item.title: Boolean combinations of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2412.19551v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Boolean combinations allow combining given combinatorial objects to obtain new, potentially more complicated, objects. In this paper, we initiate a systematic study of this idea applied to graphs. In order to understand expressive power and limitations of boolean combinations in this context, we investigate how they affect different combinatorial and structural properties of graphs, in particular $\chi$-boundedness, as well as characterize the structure of boolean combinations of graphs from various classes.
item.dc:creator: Sarosh Adenwalla, Samuel Braunfeld, John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev

item.title: Generalized Bicycle Codes with Low Connectivity: Minimum Distance Bounds and Competitive Circuit-Level Performance
item.description: arXiv:2508.09082v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present new upper and lower bounds on the minimum distance of certain generalized bicycle (GB) codes that go beyond the capabilities of techniques based on classical codes. These bounds are shown to capture the true minimum distance for specific subclasses within the GB family. In particular, we demonstrate the existence of two highly degenerate GB code families with parameters $[\![d^2+1,2,d]\!]_2$ for odd $d \geq 3$ and $[\![d^2,2,d]\!]_2$ for even $d \geq 4$, both having qubit connectivity of four, similar to that of surface codes. For the odd-distance family, we analyze the structure of low-weight logical Pauli operators and establish the existence of a fault-tolerant logical CNOT gate between the two logical qubits, achievable via a simple relabeling of data qubits. Next, using nearly self-inverse polynomials, we extend our results to construct an infinite class of connectivity-six GB codes with an improved rate. For GB codes based on these polynomials, we further present a technique to realize transversal logical CNOT gates via data-qubit permutations. We further construct syndrome extraction schemes for our connectivity four GB families that avoid reductions in minimum distance due to circuit-level faults propagating from check qubits to data qubits. Finally, we numerically evaluate the logical error rate performance of the mentioned connectivity four families of GB codes under circuit-level noise, obtaining thresholds comparable to those of rotated surface codes.
item.dc:creator: Reza Dastbasteh, Olatz Sanz Larrarte, Arun John Moncy, Paul Schnabl, Pedro M. Crespo, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Ruben M. Otxoa

item.title: A characterization of interval nest digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2603.08585v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A digraph consisting of a set of vertices $V$ and a set of arcs $E$ is called an interval digraph if there exists a family of closed intervals $\{I_u,J_u\}_{u \in V}$ such that $uv$ is an arc if and only if the intersection of $I_u$ and $J_v$ is non-empty. Interval digraphs naturally generalize interval graphs, by extending the classical interval intersection model to directed graphs. Several subclasses of interval digraphs have been studied in the literature-such as balanced, chronological and catch interval digraphs-each characterized by admitting interval representations that satisfy specific restrictions. Among these, interval nest digraphs are the ones that admit an interval representation in which $J_u$ is contained in $I_u$ for all vertices $u$ of $V$. In this work, we provide a complete characterization of interval nest digraphs in terms of vertex linear orderings with forbidden patterns, which we call nest orderings. This result completes the picture of vertex-ordering characterizations among the main subclasses of interval digraphs.
item.dc:creator: Ayel\'en Alcantar, Flavia Bonomo, Guillermo Dur\'an, Nina Pardal

item.title: Sharp Bounds on the Number of Small Cuts
item.description: arXiv:2609.10255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A $k$-cut of an undirected graph is a minimal edge set whose removal leaves at least $k$ connected components, and its cost is the sum of its edge costs. Write $\lambda_k$ for the minimum cost of a $k$-cut. For fixed $k\ge2$ and $\alpha\ge1$, we show that in any $n$-vertex graph with $n\ge k$ and nonnegative edge costs, the number of $k$-cuts of cost strictly below $\alpha\lambda_k$ is $O(n^{\lceil\alpha k\rceil-1})$. This implies an $O(n^{\lfloor\alpha k\rfloor})$ bound for $k$-cuts of cost at most $\alpha\lambda_k$, sharpening the $O(n^{\alpha k})$ bound of Gupta, Harris, Lee and Li. For $k=2$, our strict bound resolves a conjecture of Henzinger and Williamson and an open question of Karger. The exponent $\lceil\alpha k\rceil-1$ is optimal for $k$-cuts for every $k\ge2$ and $\alpha>1$.
item.dc:creator: Yu Cong, Chao Xu

item.title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequalities via Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.24687v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Isoperimetric inequalities on the Boolean hypercube play a fundamental role in the analysis of Boolean functions. These inequalities have been established primarily for the uniform measure and for biased product measures, often through Fourier-analytic or inductive arguments. We develop a curvature-based semigroup framework to establish isoperimetric inequalities for measures with weakly dependent coordinates. In particular, we show that a Dobrushin-type condition, together with marginal boundedness of the distribution, implies the local Bobkov inequality, Talagrand's $L^1$--$L^2$ and variance--surface-area inequalities, the Kahn--Kalai--Linial inequality, and the Eldan--Gross inequality. Our results apply to zero-field Ising models with interaction matrix $J$ throughout the Dobrushin uniqueness regime $\|J\|_1<1$. The framework builds on discrete Bakry--\'Emery theory and gradient estimates and can also be extended to measures on Hamming slices or hypergrids.

item.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.34273v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a conic upper bound on the asymptotic rank of every weighted graph tensor over every field. If $W$ is the logarithmic edge-weight matrix of its dimension matrix $Q$, then $$ \operatorname{MaxCut}(W)\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{WT}(Q))\le U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W). $$ Here $U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W)$ maximizes $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}W_{i,j}P_{i,j}$ over nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrices $P$ such that $J-2P$ is copositive and $P_{i,j}\le P_{i,k}+P_{k,j}$ for all distinct vertices. The matrix $J$ is all-one, and copositivity means nonnegativity of the quadratic form on nonnegative vectors. Our starting point extends OpenAI's polynomial multiplication method and its subsequent arbitrary-field developments from three tensor legs to arbitrary order. We prove $$ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n))\le\frac{n^2}{4}. $$ The edge exponent is at most $n/(2(n-1))$ and tends to the optimal value $1/2$, improving the previous Coppersmith--Winograd bounds and answering Question 1.3.1 of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. The bounds coincide for every even $n$. For every odd $m\ge3$, the theorem gives $\log_2\widetilde R_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{GT}_2(C_m))\le m-1+1/(m+1)$, improving the previous cycle bound with a gap of only $1/(m+1)$ above the maximum cut. On weighted triangles, the program recovers the rectangular matrix multiplication curve of Uzna'nski and Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam. The CP and semidefinite programs, with or without path constraints, all have value $9/4$ on the unweighted triangle, giving this upper bound a natural conic interpretation. Further applications give explicit bounds for complete multipartite graphs, split graphs, and wheels, including new cases of maximum-cut equality.
